chunks: And they said: 'O sorcerer, call for us your Lord on account of what He has pledged with you. We shall certainly be guided.'
ai.seo_question: What did the people of Pharaoh ask Prophet Musa to do in exchange for following him?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Ta-Ha, the court of Pharaoh addresses Musa (AS) as a 'sorcerer' yet pragmatically requests he invoke his Lord based on the 'covenant' (‘ahd) established with him, promising guidance in return. Shia exegetes often interpret this 'covenant' as the divine promise or authority granted to Musa, highlighting the tension between political expediency and genuine faith among the elite. This moment underscores the theme of recognizing divine power while resisting its full spiritual implications.
